svg.title: Three rungs, each added because the one below ran out of assumptions
svg.desc: Rung one assumes you can see the whole state and only one side is choosing, and solves it with integer programming plus Monte Carlo. Rung two drops the assumption that you can see what the other side chose, and solves it with counterfactual regret minimisation, producing a mixed strategy. Rung three drops the assumption that you can see the state at all, and solves it with a point-based approximation over belief states, with a leader-follower equilibrium replacing the simultaneous one because one side must commit first. Each rung keeps everything below it.
svg.text: You cannot see the state at all
SOLVER
Point-based value iteration over belief states
EQUILIBRIUM
Leader–follower, because one side must commit first
YOU GET
A policy over beliefs, and a price for committing early
Also: critical path with slack, and which question to ask next
drops: you can see the state
You cannot see what they chose
SOLVER
Counterfactual regret minimisation, 10,000 iterations
EQUILIBRIUM
Simultaneous — neither side moves first
YOU GET
A mixed strategy, and how exploitable it is
Also: hidden intent from observations, and who holds the network
drops: you can see their move
You can see everything, and only you choose
SOLVER
Integer programming, then Monte Carlo to check it
EQUILIBRIUM
None needed — nobody is playing against you
YOU GET
One optimal selection, and a win probability for it
Also: a posterior on current form, updated from results
Each rung keeps everything below it. Monte Carlo never goes away;
what changes is what you are allowed to assume before you run it.
